ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS
Except as set forth below, there have been no material changes to the risk factors disclosed in Part I, Item 1A, “Risk Factors” of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025.
We cannot assure you that our ongoing review of strategic alternatives will result in any particular outcome, and speculation and uncertainty regarding the outcome of this review may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
On October 26, 2026, we announced that our Board has initiated a formal review of strategic alternatives to maximize shareholder value and plans to consider a full range of strategic, financial, and operational alternatives, including, but not limited to, continuing to execute on the Company’s standalone strategic plan, a recapitalization, or a sale of the Company. We cannot assure you that our review of strategic alternatives will unlock shareholder value or that the review will result in any transaction or other strategic change or outcome. Furthermore, the Company may be unable to consummate effectively or efficiently or in a timely manner any strategic alternative selected by our Board. Whether the process will result in any strategic alternative being selected and ultimately implemented will depend on numerous factors, some of which are beyond our control.
The process of reviewing potential strategic alternatives, as well as implementing the alternative, if any, chosen by our Board, may be time-consuming, expensive, distracting to our management and employees, and disruptive to our business operations, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations and could result in increased volatility in our stock price. We have incurred, and expect to continue to incur, substantial expenses associated with identifying and evaluating potential strategic alternatives, including those related to legal, accounting and financial advisor fees. A considerable portion of these expenses may be incurred regardless of whether a strategic alternative is selected and consummated. In addition, the process could lead us to lose or fail to attract, retain and motivate key employees, and to lose or fail to attract customers or business partners. Furthermore, it could expose us to litigation. Even if one or more strategic alternatives are consummated, there can be no assurance that any such actions will be successful or have a positive effect on shareholder value.
We do not intend to disclose developments or provide updates on the progress or status of the strategic process until our Board deems further disclosure is appropriate or necessary. Accordingly, speculation regarding any developments related to the review of strategic alternatives and perceived uncertainties related to the future of our Company could cause the price of our common stock to fluctuate significantly. If we are unable to mitigate these or other potential risks related to the uncertainty caused by our evaluation of strategic alternatives, it could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
We are not in compliance with an NYSE continued listing standard. If we do not regain compliance, our common stock could be delisted, which could reduce the liquidity and market price of our common stock, impair our ability to raise capital, and give holders of our convertible notes the right to require us to repurchase their notes for cash, which we may not be able to do.
On October 19, 2026, we notified the NYSE that we are not in compliance with Section 802.01B of the NYSE Listed Company Manual because our average global market capitalization over a consecutive 30 trading-day period was less than $50 million and our stockholders’ equity was less than $50 million. On October 20, 2026, we received from the NYSE a non-compliance letter confirming that the Company is not in compliance with the requirement of Section 802.01B of the NYSE Listed Company Manual.
Under NYSE procedures, we must submit a business plan by December 4, 2026 that demonstrates how we intend to regain compliance with Section 802.01B within 18 months of our receipt of the letter from the NYSE. We intend to submit the plan by that date. The NYSE will review the plan. If the plan is approved, we will be subject to quarterly monitoring by the NYSE for compliance with it. If the plan is not accepted or we fail to timely submit the plan, the NYSE will begin suspension and delisting procedures. We cannot assure you that the NYSE will accept our plan, that we will be able to carry it out, or that we will regain compliance within the cure period. Whether we regain compliance depends in part on factors outside our control, including the market price of our common stock.
Even if the NYSE accepts our plan, it may begin delisting procedures before the end of the cure period in some circumstances. These include:
•our failure to meet material aspects of the plan or any quarterly milestones;
51

•our average global market capitalization falling below $15 million over a consecutive 30 trading-day period, a deficiency for which no cure period is available;
•our failure to cure, within the applicable period, a deficiency arising from an average closing price below $1.00 over a consecutive 30 trading-day period; or
•our failure to meet any other NYSE continued listing requirement.
Our ability to carry out any plan we submit to the NYSE may be adversely impacted by our Board’s ongoing review of strategic alternatives. Refer to “We cannot assure you that our ongoing review of strategic alternatives will result in any particular outcome, and speculation and uncertainty regarding the outcome of this review may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations” above, for information about risks related to the ongoing strategic review.
If our common stock is delisted from the NYSE, we expect it would trade, if at all, on an over-the-counter market. Delisting could, among other things:
•reduce the liquidity and market price of our common stock;
•reduce the number of investors willing to hold or buy our common stock, including institutional investors whose policies do not permit investment in securities that are not listed on a national securities exchange;
•result in our common stock being treated as a “penny stock,” which would require brokers trading in our common stock to follow more restrictive rules;
•reduce analyst and media coverage of the Company;
•limit our ability to raise capital on acceptable terms, or at all, including through our at-the-market equity offering program;
•end the exemption from state securities registration requirements that applies to securities listed on a national securities exchange;
•make it harder to attract and retain employees through equity awards; and
•harm our reputation with customers, suppliers and other business partners.
In addition, a delisting of our common stock would generally constitute a “fundamental change” under the indentures governing our 2028 Convertible Notes and 2030 Convertible Notes. Holders would then have the right to require us to repurchase their notes for cash at 100% of principal plus accrued and unpaid interest to, but excluding, the repurchase date. As of September 30, 2026, $68.2 million aggregate principal amount of the 2028 Convertible Notes and $118.7 million aggregate principal amount of the 2030 Convertible Notes were outstanding. We may not have enough cash to make these repurchases. Our failure to do so would be an event of default under the applicable indenture and under the indenture governing our 2030 Senior Secured Notes, which would permit the trustee or the holders of at least 25% in principal amount of those notes to declare them, together with the applicable premium, immediately due and payable.
There is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern, which may adversely affect our ability to obtain financing, our relationships with customers and suppliers, and the value of our securities.
We have a substantial amount of indebtedness, including $346.9 million in aggregate principal amount outstanding as of September 30, 2026, and we expect to pay approximately $23.0 million in cash interest over the next twelve months. We have a history of net losses and negative operating cash flows. Based on our current forecast, our existing cash and cash equivalents, together with cash expected to be generated from operations, are not expected to be sufficient to fund our operations and meet our debt service obligations for at least the next twelve months from the date of issuance of our condensed consolidated financial statements. As a result, management has concluded that there is substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.
We are pursuing actions intended to improve our liquidity and reduce our leverage. These actions depend in significant part on factors outside our control, including conditions in the capital markets and to agree to terms acceptable to us. We cannot assure you that we will complete any of these actions on acceptable terms, on a timely basis, or at all, or that, if completed, they will be sufficient to alleviate substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern.
The going concern conclusion, and the perception of our financial condition that it may create, could adversely affect our business in a number of ways. Customers may be reluctant to enter into or renew contracts with us, particularly long-term service and software arrangements, and suppliers and other counterparties may require more restrictive payment terms, letters of credit, or other credit support. It may also make it more difficult or costly for us to raise capital or refinance our debt, and could adversely affect our ability to attract and retain employees.
If we are unable to obtain sufficient financing or restructure our indebtedness, we may be required to significantly curtail or cease operations, sell assets on unfavorable terms, or seek protection under applicable bankruptcy or insolvency laws. In any such event, holders of our common stock and other securities could lose all or a substantial part of their investment. Our
52

unaudited condensed consolidated financial statements do not include any adjustments that might result from the outcome of this uncertainty.
